samples.question: Exactly one trace in this picture is teal; every other trace is pale lavender. The teal wire is a single unbranching zigzag: it has exactly two ends, it turns a right angle at every dark square stud between them, and all ten of its straight runs are the same length. Exactly one end of the teal wire sits in a crimson pad. Twenty-five short teal barbs stick straight out of the wire, two or three on each straight run, each barb sticking out of exactly one of the two sides of the run it belongs to. Carry out this operation. Start at the end in the crimson pad and walk along the teal wire to its other end. Each time you pass a barb, write 1 if that barb sticks out to your left as you are walking at that moment and 0 if it sticks out to your right; remember that your left changes with you at every turn of the wire, so the same direction on the page is your left on some runs and your right on others. Take the twenty-five bits in the order you meet the barbs and write them into a 5 by 5 grid, the first five bits into the top row left to right, the next five into the second row, and so on to the bottom row, then mark every grid position holding a 1. Compare the marked positions with these five symbols on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the whole centre row together with the whole centre column, 'ex' is the two whole diagonals, 'tee' is the whole top row together with the centre column below it, 'tack' is the whole bottom row together with the centre column above it, and 'ell' is the whole left column together with the whole bottom row. Each of those symbols marks exactly 9 of the 25 positions, and the answer is the one symbol that differs from your marked positions in the fewest positions; up to three positions may disagree. The shape the wire itself traces on the page is not the symbol, the lavender traces are decoration, and only your own left and right while walking the wire decide the bits. Which symbol is it? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tack, tee.
